sanskrit: aśvatthāmā tu saṃkruddho laghuhastaḥ pratāpavān ghaṭotkacam abhikruddhaṃ bibheda daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: But Aśvatthāman, enraged, nimble of hand and full of majesty, pierced the furious Ghaṭotkaca with ten arrows.

sanskrit: ghaṭotkaco 'tividdhas tu droṇaputreṇa marmasu cakraṃ śatasahasrāram agṛhṇād vyathito bhṛśam
english: Ghaṭotkaca, struck deep in his vital parts by Droṇa's son and sorely pained, seized a discus fitted with a hundred thousand spokes.

sanskrit: kṣurāntaṃ bālasūryābhaṃ maṇivajravibhūṣitam aśvatthāmnas tu cikṣepa bhaimasenir jighāṃsayā
english: Its rim keen as a razor, gleaming like the rising sun and adorned with gems and diamonds, the son of Bhīmasena hurled it at Aśvatthāman, eager to slay him.

sanskrit: vegena mahatā gacchad vikṣiptaṃ drauṇinā śaraiḥ abhāgyasyeva saṃkalpas tan moghaṃ nyapatad bhuvi
english: Speeding on with mighty force, it was deflected by Droṇa's son with his arrows; like the resolve of a luckless man, it fell to the ground in vain.

sanskrit: ghaṭotkacas tatas tūrṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā cakraṃ nipātitam drauṇiṃ prācchādayad bāṇaiḥ svarbhānur iva bhāskaram
english: Then Ghaṭotkaca, seeing the discus struck down, swiftly covered Droṇa's son with arrows, as Svarbhānu covers the sun.

sanskrit: ghaṭotkacasutaḥ śrīmān bhinnāñjanacayopamaḥ rurodha drauṇim āyāntaṃ prabhañjanam ivādrirāṭ
english: The glorious son of Ghaṭotkaca, like a heap of broken collyrium, blocked the advancing son of Droṇa as a king of mountains withstands the storm-wind.

sanskrit: pautreṇa bhīmasenasya śaraiḥ so 'ñjanaparvaṇā babhau meghena dhārābhir girir merur ivārditaḥ
english: Assailed by the arrows of Bhīmasena's grandson, Añjanaparvan, he shone like Mount Meru tormented by the torrents of a cloud.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmā tv asaṃbhrānto rudropendrendravikramaḥ dhvajam ekena bāṇena cicchedāñjanaparvaṇaḥ
english: But Aśvatthāman, unshaken, with the valor of Rudra, Upendra, and Indra, severed the banner of Añjanaparvan with a single arrow.

sanskrit: dvābhyāṃ tu rathayantāraṃ tribhiś cāsya triveṇukam dhanur ekena ciccheda caturbhiś caturo hayān
english: With two he felled the charioteer, with three the triple shaft of the car; with one he cut his bow, and with four he slew his four horses.

sanskrit: virathasyodyataṃ hastād dhemabindubhir ācitam viśikhena sutīkṣṇena khaḍgam asya dvidhākarot
english: As the carless warrior raised in his hand a sword studded with golden drops, with a keen-pointed shaft he clove it in two.

sanskrit: gadā hemāṅgadā rājaṃs tūrṇaṃ haiḍimbasūnunā bhrāmyotkṣiptā śaraiḥ sāpi drauṇinābhyāhatāpatat
english: A mace banded with gold, O king, was swiftly whirled aloft and flung by Haiḍimba's son; but it too, struck by the arrows of Droṇa's son, fell.

sanskrit: tato 'ntarikṣam utpatya kālamegha ivonnadan vavarṣāñjanaparvā sa drumavarṣaṃ nabhastalāt
english: Then, springing into the sky and roaring like a cloud of doom, Añjanaparvan rained down a shower of trees from the vault of heaven.

sanskrit: tato māyādharaṃ drauṇir ghaṭotkacasutaṃ divi mārgaṇair abhivivyādha ghanaṃ sūrya ivāṃśubhiḥ
english: Then Droṇa's son pierced the illusion-wielding son of Ghaṭotkaca in the sky with his shafts, as the sun pierces a cloud with its rays.

sanskrit: so 'vatīrya punas tasthau rathe hemapariṣkṛte mahīdhara ivātyuccaḥ śrīmān añjanaparvataḥ
english: Descending, he again took his stand upon his gold-wrought car, the glorious Añjanaparvan, lofty as a mountain.

sanskrit: tam ayasmayavarmāṇaṃ drauṇir bhīmātmajātmajam jaghānāñjanaparvāṇaṃ maheśvara ivāndhakam
english: Droṇa's son slew that Añjanaparvan, the grandson of Bhīma, clad in iron mail, as Maheśvara slew Andhaka.

sanskrit: atha dṛṣṭvā hataṃ putram aśvatthāmnā mahābalam drauṇeḥ sakāśam abhyetya roṣāt pracalitāṅgadaḥ
english: Then, seeing his mighty son slain by Aśvatthāman, he came near to Droṇa's son, his armlets trembling with rage.

sanskrit: prāha vākyam asaṃbhrānto vīraṃ śāradvatīsutam dahantaṃ pāṇḍavānīkaṃ vanam agnim ivoddhatam
english: Unflinching, he spoke these words to the hero, the son of Śāradvatī's daughter, who was consuming the Pāṇḍava host like a raging fire a forest:

sanskrit: tiṣṭha tiṣṭha na me jīvan droṇaputra gamiṣyasi tvām adya nihaniṣyāmi krauñcam agnisuto yathā
english: "Stay, stay! You shall not depart alive from me, O son of Droṇa. This day I shall slay you as the fire-god's son slew Krauñca."

sanskrit: aśvatthāmovāca gaccha vatsa sahānyais tvaṃ yudhyasvāmaravikrama na hi putreṇa haiḍimbe pitā nyāyyaṃ prabādhitum
english: Aśvatthāman said: "Go, child, and fight with the others, you whose valor is that of the immortals; for it is not fitting, O son of Haiḍimbā, that a father be assailed by a son."

sanskrit: kāmaṃ khalu na me roṣo haiḍimbe vidyate tvayi kiṃ tu roṣānvito jantur hanyād ātmānam apy uta
english: "Truly I bear no wrath toward you, O son of Haiḍimbā; yet a creature filled with rage may slay even his own self."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca śrutvaitat krodhatāmrākṣaḥ putraśokasamanvitaḥ aśvatthāmānam āyasto bhaimasenir abhāṣata
english: Saṃjaya said: Hearing this, his eyes coppery with anger and stricken with grief for his son, the son of Bhīmasena, sorely vexed, addressed Aśvatthāman:

sanskrit: kim ahaṃ kātaro drauṇe pṛthagjana ivāhave bhīmāt khalv aham utpannaḥ kurūṇāṃ vipule kule
english: "Am I a coward, O son of Droṇa, like a common man in battle? Indeed I am sprung from Bhīma, in the vast lineage of the Kurus."

sanskrit: pāṇḍavānām ahaṃ putraḥ samareṣv anivartinām rakṣasām adhirājo 'haṃ daśagrīvasamo bale
english: "I am a son of the Pāṇḍavas, who never turn back in battle; I am overlord of the rākṣasas, equal in strength to the ten-necked one."

sanskrit: tiṣṭha tiṣṭha na me jīvan droṇaputra gamiṣyasi yuddhaśraddhām ahaṃ te 'dya vineṣyāmi raṇājire
english: "Stay, stay! You shall not depart alive from me, O son of Droṇa. This day I shall drive out your lust for battle on the field of war."

sanskrit: ity uktvā roṣatāmrākṣo rākṣasaḥ sumahābalaḥ drauṇim abhyadravat kruddho gajendram iva kesarī
english: Having spoken thus, his eyes coppery with rage, the rākṣasa of mighty strength rushed in fury upon Droṇa's son, as a lion upon a lordly elephant.

sanskrit: rathākṣamātrair iṣubhir abhyavarṣad ghaṭotkacaḥ rathinām ṛṣabhaṃ drauṇiṃ dhārābhir iva toyadaḥ
english: Ghaṭotkaca rained upon Droṇa's son, the bull among chariot-warriors, arrows as large as chariot-axles, as a raincloud pours down its torrents.

sanskrit: śaravṛṣṭiṃ śarair drauṇir aprāptāṃ tāṃ vyaśātayat tato 'ntarikṣe bāṇānāṃ saṃgrāmo 'nya ivābhavat
english: Droṇa's son shattered that shower of arrows with his own arrows before it reached him; then in mid-air there arose, as it were, another battle of shafts.

sanskrit: athāstrasaṃgharṣakṛtair visphuliṅgaiḥ samābabhau vibhāvarīmukhe vyoma khadyotair iva citritam
english: Then with the sparks struck out by the clashing of weapons, the sky at the threshold of night gleamed as though painted bright with fireflies.

sanskrit: niśāmya nihatāṃ māyāṃ drauṇinā raṇamāninā ghaṭotkacas tato māyāṃ sasarjāntarhitaḥ punaḥ
english: Seeing his illusion destroyed by the battle-proud son of Droṇa, Ghaṭotkaca then, vanishing once more, conjured up another illusion.

sanskrit: so 'bhavad girir atyuccaḥ śikharais tarusaṃkaṭaiḥ śūlaprāsāsimusalajalaprasravaṇo mahān
english: He became a towering mountain, its peaks dense with trees, vast, streaming with cascades of spears, javelins, swords, and clubs.

sanskrit: tam añjanacayaprakhyaṃ drauṇir dṛṣṭvā mahīdharam prapatadbhiś ca bahubhiḥ śastrasaṃghair na cukṣubhe
english: Seeing that mountain, dark as a heap of collyrium, and the many masses of weapons falling from it, Droṇa's son was not shaken.

sanskrit: tataḥ smayann iva drauṇir vajram astram udīrayat sa tenāstreṇa śailendraḥ kṣiptaḥ kṣipram anaśyata
english: Then Droṇa's son, smiling as it were, sent forth the thunderbolt weapon; struck by that weapon, the king of mountains swiftly vanished.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa toyado bhūtvā nīlaḥ sendrāyudho divi aśmavṛṣṭibhir atyugro drauṇim ācchādayad raṇe
english: Then, becoming a dark raincloud arched with the rainbow in the sky, most fierce, he covered Droṇa's son in battle with showers of stones.

sanskrit: atha saṃdhāya vāyavyam astram astravidāṃ varaḥ vyadhamad droṇatanayo nīlameghaṃ samutthitam
english: Then the son of Droṇa, foremost of those who know weapons, fitting the wind-weapon to his bow, scattered the dark cloud that had risen up.

sanskrit: sa mārgaṇagaṇair drauṇir diśaḥ pracchādya sarvataḥ śataṃ rathasahasrāṇāṃ jaghāna dvipadāṃ varaḥ
english: Droṇa's son, that best of men, covering all the quarters on every side with his hosts of arrows, slew a hundred thousand chariots.

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvā punar āyāntaṃ rathenāyatakārmukam ghaṭotkacam asaṃbhrāntaṃ rākṣasair bahubhir vṛtam
english: He saw Ghaṭotkaca coming again on his car, his bow drawn wide, undaunted, surrounded by many rākṣasas —

sanskrit: siṃhaśārdūlasadṛśair mattadviradavikramaiḥ gajasthaiś ca rathasthaiś ca vājipṛṣṭhagatair api
english: like lions and tigers, with the prowess of rutting elephants, mounted on elephants, on chariots, and on the backs of horses,

sanskrit: vivṛtāsyaśirogrīvair haiḍimbānucaraiḥ saha paulastyair yātudhānaiś ca tāmasaiś cogravikramaiḥ
english: their mouths, heads, and necks gaping wide — together with the followers of Haiḍimbā, with Paulastya demons and dark-natured fiends of fierce valor.

sanskrit: nānāśastradharair vīrair nānākavacabhūṣaṇaiḥ mahābalair bhīmaravaiḥ saṃrambhodvṛttalocanaiḥ
english: with heroes bearing weapons of every kind, decked in armor of every kind, mighty in strength, terrible of cry, their eyes rolling in fury.

sanskrit: upasthitais tato yuddhe rākṣasair yuddhadurmadaiḥ viṣaṇṇam abhisaṃprekṣya putraṃ te drauṇir abravīt
english: Then, beholding your son disheartened at the rākṣasas, frenzied for battle, drawn up for the fight, Droṇa's son said:

sanskrit: tiṣṭha duryodhanādya tvaṃ na kāryaḥ saṃbhramas tvayā sahaibhir bhrātṛbhir vīraiḥ pārthivaiś cendravikramaiḥ
english: "Stand firm, Duryodhana, this day, and let no agitation be felt by you, together with these heroic brothers and these kings of Indra's valor."

sanskrit: nihaniṣyāmy amitrāṃs te na tavāsti parājayaḥ satyaṃ te pratijānāmi paryāśvāsaya vāhinīm
english: "I shall slay your foes; there is no defeat for you. Truly I promise you this — reassure your army."

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca na tv etad adbhutaṃ manye yat te mahad idaṃ manaḥ asmāsu ca parā bhaktis tava gautaminandana
english: Duryodhana said: "I think it no wonder that this mind of yours is so great, and that your devotion to us is supreme, O joy of Gautama's line."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca aśvatthāmānam uktvaivaṃ tataḥ saubalam abravīt vṛtaḥ śatasahasreṇa rathānāṃ raṇaśobhinām
english: Saṃjaya said: Having thus addressed Aśvatthāman, he then spoke to Subala's son, encircled by a hundred thousand chariots that graced the battlefield:

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭyā gajasahasraiś ca prayāhi tvaṃ dhanaṃjayam karṇaś ca vṛṣasenaś ca kṛpo nīlas tathaiva ca
english: "With sixty thousand elephants go forth against Dhanaṃjaya — Karṇa and Vṛṣasena and Kṛpa and Nīla as well,"

sanskrit: udīcyāḥ kṛtavarmā ca purumitraḥ śrutārpaṇaḥ duḥśāsano nikumbhaś ca kuṇḍabhedī urukramaḥ
english: "the Northerners and Kṛtavarman, Purumitra, Śrutārpaṇa, Duḥśāsana and Nikumbha, Kuṇḍabhedin, Urukrama,"

sanskrit: puraṃjayo dṛḍharathaḥ patākī hemapaṅkajaḥ śalyāruṇīndrasenāś ca saṃjayo vijayo jayaḥ
english: "Puraṃjaya, Dṛḍharatha, Patākin, Hemapaṅkaja, Śalya, Aruṇi, and Indrasena, Saṃjaya, Vijaya, Jaya,"

sanskrit: kamalākṣaḥ puruḥ krāthī jayavarmā sudarśanaḥ ete tvām anuyāsyanti pattīnām ayutāni ṣaṭ
english: "Kamalākṣa, Puru, Krāthin, Jayavarman, Sudarśana — these shall follow you, with sixty thousand foot-soldiers."

sanskrit: jahi bhīmaṃ yamau cobhau dharmarājaṃ ca mātula asurān iva devendro jayāśā me tvayi sthitā
english: "Slay Bhīma and both the twins and the King of Righteousness, O uncle, as the lord of the gods slew the asuras; my hope of victory rests in you."

sanskrit: dāritān drauṇinā bāṇair bhṛśaṃ vikṣatavigrahān jahi mātula kaunteyān asurān iva pāvakiḥ
english: "Slay the sons of Kuntī, O uncle, torn by the arrows of Droṇa's son and grievously wounded in body, as the fire-god's son slew the asuras."

sanskrit: evam ukto yayau śīghraṃ putreṇa tava saubalaḥ piprīṣus te sutān rājan didhakṣuś caiva pāṇḍavān
english: Thus addressed by your son, Subala's son went forth swiftly, eager to please your sons, O king, and longing to burn up the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: atha pravavṛte yuddhaṃ drauṇirākṣasayor mṛdhe vibhāvaryāṃ sutumulaṃ śakraprahrādayor iva
english: Then in the night the battle between Droṇa's son and the rākṣasa grew most tumultuous on the field, like that between Śakra and Prahrāda.

sanskrit: tato ghaṭotkaco bāṇair daśabhir gautamīsutam jaghānorasi saṃkruddho viṣāgnipratimair dṛḍhaiḥ
english: Then Ghaṭotkaca, enraged, struck the son of Gautamī in the chest with ten firm arrows, like venom and fire.

sanskrit: sa tair abhyāhato gāḍhaṃ śarair bhīmasuteritaiḥ cacāla rathamadhyastho vātoddhūta iva drumaḥ
english: Struck hard by those arrows loosed by Bhīma's son, he reeled as he stood in the midst of his car, like a tree shaken by the wind.

sanskrit: bhūyaś cāñjalikenāsya mārgaṇena mahāprabham drauṇihastasthitaṃ cāpaṃ cicchedāśu ghaṭotkacaḥ
english: And again, with an añjalika shaft, Ghaṭotkaca swiftly cut the bright bow that rested in the hand of Droṇa's son.

sanskrit: tato 'nyad drauṇir ādāya dhanur bhārasahaṃ mahat vavarṣa viśikhāṃs tīkṣṇān vāridhārā ivāmbudaḥ
english: Then Droṇa's son, taking up another great bow that could bear the strain, rained down sharp shafts as a raincloud pours its torrents.

sanskrit: tataḥ śāradvatīputraḥ preṣayām āsa bhārata suvarṇapuṅkhāñ śatrughnān khacarān khacarān prati
english: Then the son of Śāradvatī's daughter, O Bhārata, sent forth foe-destroying, gold-feathered, sky-ranging shafts against the sky-rangers.

sanskrit: tadbāṇair arditaṃ yūthaṃ rakṣasāṃ pīnavakṣasām siṃhair iva babhau mattaṃ gajānām ākulaṃ kulam
english: That troop of broad-chested rākṣasas, tormented by his arrows, appeared like a frenzied herd of elephants thrown into disarray by lions.

sanskrit: vidhamya rākṣasān bāṇaiḥ sāśvasūtarathān vibhuḥ dadāha bhagavān vahnir bhūtānīva yugakṣaye
english: Scattering the rākṣasas with their horses, drivers, and cars, the mighty one consumed them as the blessed Fire consumes all beings at the world's end.

sanskrit: sa dagdhvākṣauhiṇīṃ bāṇair nairṛtān ruruce bhṛśam pureva tripuraṃ dagdhvā divi devo maheśvaraḥ
english: Having burned with his arrows a whole akṣauhiṇī of the night-roving demons, he shone resplendent, as of old the god Maheśvara shone in heaven when he burned Tripura.

sanskrit: yugānte sarvabhūtāni dagdhveva vasur ulbaṇaḥ rarāja jayatāṃ śreṣṭho droṇaputras tavāhitān
english: Like the fierce Fire that has burned up all beings at the end of an age, Droṇa's son, best of the victorious, shone forth, having burned your foes.

sanskrit: teṣu rājasahasreṣu pāṇḍaveyeṣu bhārata nainaṃ nirīkṣituṃ kaś cic chaknoti drauṇim āhave ṛte ghaṭotkacād vīrād rākṣasendrān mahābalāt
english: Among those thousands of kings on the Pāṇḍava side, O Bhārata, none could so much as look upon Droṇa's son in battle, save the hero Ghaṭotkaca, the mighty lord of the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: sa punar bharataśreṣṭha krodhād raktāntalocanaḥ talaṃ talena saṃhatya saṃdaśya daśanacchadam svasūtam abravīt kruddho droṇaputrāya māṃ vaha
english: He once more, O best of the Bharatas, his eyes red-cornered with wrath, clapping palm against palm and biting his lip, said in fury to his charioteer, "Bear me toward the son of Droṇa."

sanskrit: sa yayau ghorarūpeṇa tena jaitrapatākinā dvairathaṃ droṇaputreṇa punar apy arisūdanaḥ
english: On that car of dreadful form, bannered with victory-pennons, the slayer of foes went forth once more to single combat with the son of Droṇa.

sanskrit: sa cikṣepa tataḥ kruddho droṇaputrāya rākṣasaḥ aṣṭacakrāṃ mahāraudrām aśanīṃ rudranirmitām
english: Then the rākṣasa in his fury hurled at the son of Droṇa a thunderbolt of dreadful might, eight-wheeled and fashioned by Rudra.

sanskrit: tām avaplutya jagrāha drauṇir nyasya rathe dhanuḥ cikṣepa caināṃ tasyaiva syandanāt so 'vapupluve
english: Droṇa's son, leaping down and laying his bow upon the car, caught it, and flung it back; whereupon the rākṣasa sprang from his own chariot.

sanskrit: sāśvasūtadhvajaṃ vāhaṃ bhasma kṛtvā mahāprabhā viveśa vasudhāṃ bhittvā sāśanir bhṛśadāruṇā
english: Reducing the car with its horses, driver, and banner to ashes, that thunderbolt of great splendor and dreadful fierceness clove the earth and entered it.

sanskrit: drauṇes tat karma dṛṣṭvā tu sarvabhūtāny apūjayan yad avaplutya jagrāha ghorāṃ śaṃkaranirmitām
english: Beholding that deed of Droṇa's son — how, leaping down, he had caught the dreadful weapon fashioned by Śaṃkara — all beings did him honor.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnarathaṃ gatvā bhaimasenis tato nṛpa mumoca niśitān bāṇān punar drauṇer mahorasi
english: Then, O king, the son of Bhīmasena, going to the car of Dhṛṣṭadyumna, loosed sharp arrows once again into the broad chest of Droṇa's son.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumno 'py asaṃbhrānto mumocāśīviṣopamān suvarṇapuṅkhān viśikhān droṇaputrasya vakṣasi
english: Dhṛṣṭadyumna too, undaunted, loosed gold-feathered shafts like serpents' venom into the breast of Droṇa's son.

sanskrit: tato mumoca nārācān drauṇis tābhyāṃ sahasraśaḥ tāv apy agniśikhāprakhyair jaghnatus tasya mārgaṇān
english: Then Droṇa's son loosed iron shafts by the thousand against those two; and they in turn struck down his arrows with shafts bright as tongues of flame.

sanskrit: atitīvram abhūd yuddhaṃ tayoḥ puruṣasiṃhayoḥ yodhānāṃ prītijananaṃ drauṇeś ca bharatarṣabha
english: Most fierce grew the battle between those two lions among men and Droṇa's son, O bull of the Bharatas, gladdening the hearts of the warriors.

sanskrit: tato rathasahasreṇa dviradānāṃ śatais tribhiḥ ṣaḍbhir vājisahasraiś ca bhīmas taṃ deśam āvrajat
english: Then with a thousand chariots, three hundred elephants, and six thousand horses, Bhīma came to that place.

sanskrit: tato bhīmātmajaṃ rakṣo dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ ca sānugam ayodhayata dharmātmā drauṇir akliṣṭakarmakṛt
english: Then the righteous son of Droṇa, untiring in his deeds, gave battle to Bhīma's son the rākṣasa and to Dhṛṣṭadyumna with his followers.

sanskrit: tatrādbhutatamaṃ drauṇir darśayām āsa vikramam aśakyaṃ kartum anyena sarvabhūteṣu bhārata
english: There Droṇa's son displayed a most wondrous valor, such as could not be matched by any other among all beings, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: nimeṣāntaramātreṇa sāśvasūtarathadvipām akṣauhiṇīṃ rākṣasānāṃ śitair bāṇair aśātayat
english: In the mere span between two blinks of an eye, with his sharp arrows he laid low a whole akṣauhiṇī of rākṣasas, with their horses, drivers, cars, and elephants.

sanskrit: miṣato bhīmasenasya haiḍimbeḥ pārṣatasya ca yamayor dharmaputrasya vijayasyācyutasya ca
english: Before the very eyes of Bhīmasena, of Haiḍimbā's son, of Pārṣata, of the twins, of the son of Dharma, of Vijaya, and of Acyuta.

sanskrit: pragāḍham añjogatibhir nārācair abhitāḍitāḥ nipetur dviradā bhūmau dviśṛṅgā iva parvatāḥ
english: Smitten deep by straight-flying iron shafts, the elephants fell to the earth like twin-peaked mountains.

sanskrit: nikṛttair hastihastaiś ca vicaladbhir itas tataḥ rarāja vasudhā kīrṇā visarpadbhir ivoragaiḥ
english: With elephants' trunks cut off and writhing here and there, the earth, strewn with them, gleamed as though with crawling serpents.

sanskrit: kṣiptaiḥ kāñcanadaṇḍaiś ca nṛpacchatraiḥ kṣitir babhau dyaur ivoditacandrārkā grahākīrṇā yugakṣaye
english: With royal parasols on golden staves flung down, the earth shone like the sky strewn with planets, the moon and sun risen together at the dissolution of an age.
